question: Which of the following is the green algae?
solution:
__
 
• The correct option is **Chlorophyceae__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The members of Chlorophyceae are commonly called green algae.
 
• They may be **u****nicellular, colonial, or filamentous**.
 
• They are usually grass-green due to the dominance of pigments **Chlorophyll a **and **b**.
 
• They have storage bodies called **Pyrenoids** located in the chloroplast.
 
• Green algae usually have a rigid cell wall made of the **inner layer of cellulose **and the outer layer of pectose.
 
• Usually, they reproduce by the method of **Fragmentation**.**​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

**Phaeophyceae**

 
• Phaeophyceae are **Brown Algae** found primarily in **marine habitats**.
 
• They range from simple **branched **and **filamentous.**
 
• They possess **Chlorophyll a, c, carotenoids**, and, xanthophylls.
 
• They vary in color from olive green to various shades of brown depending on the number of xanthophylls.
 
• The vegetative cells have a cellulosic wall usually covered on the outside by a **gelatinous coating of algin.**
 
• They reproduce **sexually**, it may be isogamous, or anisogamous.

**Rhodophyceae**

 
• Rhodophyceae are commonly called **Red Algae** because of the predominance of the red pigment.
 
• The majority of the red algae are **marine** with greater concentrations found in warmer areas.
 
• They are **multicellular **and **complex** in body structure.
 
• The food is stored as **Floridian**** Starch, **similar to amylopectin and glycogen in structure.
 
• The red algae usually reproduce **vegetatively** by **fragmentation**.

**Liverworts**

 
• Liverworts are **Bryophytes **commonly found in **moist shaded** areas in the hills.
 
• They are also called the **amphibians** of the plant kingdom because they can live in soil but are dependent on water for **Sexual Reproduction**.
 
• The plant body of bryophytes is like **Thallus or Erect**.
 
• They lack **true roots**, stems, or leaves but may process root-like, leaf-like, or stem-like structures.
